themes.theme: LTL freight volume inflection after a 3-year freight recession
themes.evidence: Saia Q2 2026 (Jul 30): tonnage/workday +8.4%, shipments +4.4%, contract renewals +10.7%, EPS +31%, yet stock -12% on a Q3 margin guide; Saia July and August 2026 volumes above 2025 (Simply Wall St, Sep 16). XPO August tonnage/day +3.7% YoY (8-K, Sep 3). FedEx Freight 10-K (Aug 5) still guides to industrial softness through CY2026, so consensus is not yet positioned for recovery. ISM manufacturing 54.5 in Sep, new orders 55.3 (First Trust, Oct 1).

themes.theme: Commercial aerospace production ramp and engine aftermarket (LEAP shop visits)
themes.evidence: Boeing moving 737 from 42 to 47/month with FAA concurrence and opened a fourth line in July 2026 (10-Q Q2 2026; CEO May 27). Airbus at 475 deliveries Jan-Aug vs 434, targeting 870 for 2026. Metalworking machinery orders +31.9% YTD, driven largely by aerospace (May 2026). Aftermarket names derated anyway: SARO -41% from its high despite a beat-and-raise.

themes.theme: Data center power equipment (gensets, power pods, switchgear, fiber)
themes.evidence: Leaders (VRT, GEV, ETN, PWR) are on the watchlist and heavily owned. But second-derivative names are de-rating while their 2027 backlog builds: Generac's data center backlog is $1.6B, $1.35B of it for 2027 delivery, against ~$450M of 2026 data center revenue. Regal Rexnord has ~$735M of E-Pod orders shipping from early 2027. Dycom's backlog is $12.2B (+53%). Several AI-infrastructure names are well below their 2026 highs (Nasdaq, Sep 4).

themes.theme: Fiber build-out: BEAD broadband plus hyperscaler long-haul and middle-mile
themes.evidence: Dycom: BEAD construction starts 'in earnest' in calendar 2027. It has over $1B of contracted long-haul/middle-mile backlog and expects 'marked acceleration' of industry activity in CY2027 (Q2 FY27 call, Aug 26, 2026). The stock fell 52% from its high on a soft Q3 guide and a $150M wireless deferral.

themes.theme: IEEPA tariff refunds and input-cost inflation
themes.evidence: Refunds of IEEPA tariffs are flowing into 2026 earnings: RRX guide includes $0.57/sh, GNRC EBITDA margin +~150bp. The market strips these out as one-offs, which flatters 2026 multiples. ISM prices paid jumped to 77.9 in September (First Trust, Oct 1), and supplier deliveries are stretched by AI demand for electrical parts and by Middle East shipping disruption.

CNH Q2 2026 (Aug 3): management says this is the trough (dealer inventory normalised, fleets ageing) but sees no evidence yet of a sustained recovery. NA tractors -16/-17% in Q2. 2026 EPS guide is $0.41-0.46, so estimates are not yet rising. Deere is already +46% off its low. Too early to pick: no estimate support.

themes.theme: Residential HVAC, pool and housing weakness
themes.evidence: RRX's PES segment fell 6.6% organically on residential HVAC and pool (Aug 5). Generac residential sales -2% in Q2. This is a known drag and is in the price of mixed names.

ideas.name: Saia Inc.
ideas.thesis: Saia is the LTL carrier with the most operating leverage to a freight recovery: it opened 20+ new terminals in 2024-26 and is filling them. Tonnage is now up high single digits, contract renewals are +10.7%, and EPS grew 31% in Q2 2026. The stock has fallen ~16% over 6 months on a one-quarter margin guide.
ideas.why_now: Q2 2026 (Jul 30) beat by $0.13 with revenue +17.1%, tonnage/workday +8.4% and OR improved to 86.9%, but the stock fell 12% on a ~100bp sequential Q3 OR guide. July and August volumes were above 2025, the 7.1% GRI went in July with 'good acceptance', the LA mix headwind has been lapped, and XPO's August tonnage turned +3.7%.

catalysts.event: Q3 2026 results, expected per Earnings Whispers (consensus ~$3.30 EPS, ~$962M revenue)
October monthly LTL operating update (tonnage/shipments per workday)
Annual GRI and contract-renewal pricing for 2027

ideas.valuation: At ~$338 (Oct 9): ~29x 2026 EPS ($11.62) and ~23x 2027 ($14.71). Saia and ODFL have typically traded around 30x+ forward through the cycle. UBS puts the LTL peer average near 37.5x on 2027 (May 2026). FedEx Freight (FDXF) is cheaper at ~21x UBS CY27 EPS of $5.45, but its volumes are shrinking and FedEx's 19.9% stake overhangs it. Balance sheet is net-debt-light: $100M debt, $84M cash.
ideas.estimate_revisions: Up. FY2026 consensus EPS was $10.61 in early April (Seeking Alpha snapshot) and ~$11.62 now (aktien.guide), about +10%, while the stock is -16% over the same period. 2027 is ~$14.71 (snippet, unconfirmed).
ideas.forward_growth: Consensus EPS ~+20-25% in 2026 (~$11.62) and ~+27% in 2027 (~$14.71). Revenue grew 17% in Q2 2026, partly from fuel surcharge. Sources: aktien.guide, Seeking Alpha snapshot, Saia Q2 2026 release and call.
ideas.priced_in: 6-month -15.8% ($401.67 on Apr 9 to ~$338). +36% from the 52-week low ($249.32), -32% from the 52-week high ($494.71). The market is pricing a margin stall, not the volume inflection. Estimates rose ~10% while the price fell, so the multiple compressed to the low end of history just as tonnage turned positive.
key_risks: Freight recovery stalls; the ISM rollover from 55.6 in July to 54.5 in September is a warning
Wage inflation: 11% salaries growth adds ~1pt to OR; fuel volatility from the Middle East conflict
Pricing competition as carriers fill post-Yellow capacity; FDXF as a newly independent, aggressive competitor
Still a premium multiple: if 2027 EPS slips, there is no valuation cushion
ideas.overlap_with_holdings: None. A pure freight/industrial-cycle name with no AI, consumer-internet or power overlap, so it diversifies a portfolio of TJX, BKNG, NFLX, VST, GOOGL, AVGO, NVDA and AMZN. Related past ideas ODFL and KNX were researched on 2026-09-25 and not picked.

ideas.name: Dycom Industries, Inc.
ideas.thesis: Dycom's revenue grew 46% (17% organic) last quarter and its backlog is a record $12.2B (+53%), yet the stock is down 52% from its May high on one soft quarterly guide and a $150M wireless deferral. Its biggest growth drivers start in calendar 2027 (BEAD construction plus hyperscaler long-haul and data-center interconnect fiber), so at ~14x next-year EPS the stock prices a peak rather than a ramp.
ideas.why_now: Q2 FY27 (Aug 26, 2026): revenue $2.01B (+45.6%), adj EPS $5.29 vs $4.68 consensus, EBITDA margin 15.7%. The stock fell ~22% that week because the Q3 EPS guide midpoint ($4.56) missed by 3%, the Communications outlook was trimmed, and ~$150M of wireless work moved into FY28. It kept sliding to ~$273, near its 52-week low, even though FY guidance was raised to $7.48-7.66B and a $150M buyback was added.

catalysts.event: Q3 FY27 results (quarter ending Oct 31): backlog conversion and first FY28 framing
BEAD construction ramp begins in earnest in calendar 2027, per management
FY28 guidance with Q4 FY27 results (deferred wireless revenue lands in FY28)

ideas.valuation: At ~$273: ~15.9x FY27 (Jan-2027) EPS (~$17.2 implied) and ~13.6x FY28 consensus (~$20.0, Zacks). That is well below Dycom's own 2025-26 range (~38x trailing P/E in July 2026 per AAII) and below specialty-contractor peers such as PWR and MTZ, which typically trade at 25x+. The average analyst target is ~$445 (Benzinga, mid-Sep).
ideas.estimate_revisions: Down slightly. The FY28 EPS estimate slipped to ~$20.01 over the last 30 days (Zacks), and targets were cut after Aug 26 (KeyBanc $610 to $423, JPM $650 to $570, Cantor $654 to $476). FY27 revenue guidance went up and the Communications segment went down.
ideas.forward_growth: Consensus EPS +43.6% in FY27 and +16.4% in FY28 (Zacks via search, Aug-Sep 2026). FY27 revenue guide is $7.48-7.66B (~+60% including acquired Building Systems). $6.47B of backlog is due within 12 months.
ideas.priced_in: 6-month -30% ($391.62 on Apr 9 to ~$273). Only +4% from the 52-week low ($263.36), -52% from the 52-week high ($566.47). The stock has fully de-rated, but the CY2027 BEAD and long-haul ramp and the backlog that is 53% higher are not in a ~14x FY28 multiple.
key_risks: Customer concentration (AT&T, Lumen, Verizon, Comcast) and timing slips like the $150M wireless deferral
BEAD funding and program rules keep changing; management warns the ~$17B addressable market could change
AI capex digestion would hit long-haul and data-center fiber demand
Integration and margin mix of the acquired Building Systems business; working-capital swings
ideas.overlap_with_holdings: Moderate. Its hyperscaler long-haul fiber exposure ties to the AI-capex theme behind GOOGL, AMZN, NVDA and AVGO, but most revenue is telecom and broadband (FTTH, BEAD). PWR on the watchlist is a related contractor; Dycom is telecom-focused rather than power.

ideas.name: Generac Holdings Inc.
ideas.thesis: Generac's data center revenue should roughly triple in 2027: $1.35B of its $1.6B data center backlog is scheduled for 2027 delivery, against ~$450M of 2026 data center revenue. A second hyperscale agreement 'at least as large as the first' is not yet in backlog. Its residential standby base is at a cyclical low. The stock trades ~20-22x 2027 EPS, below its own history and well below data-center power peers.
ideas.why_now: Q2 2026 (Jul 29): sales +11%, C&I +29% to $556M, C&I growth guide raised to low-30s%, EBITDA margin guide raised to 20-21%. About $1B of new data center orders came in over 90 days. A second hyperscale supply agreement was signed Jun 24, with 2027-28 volume terms under negotiation. Belvidere packaging capacity comes online in Q1 2027. The stock is still 24% below its high.

catalysts.event: Q3 2026 results (late Oct, date not yet confirmed): data center conversion and backlog update
Finalized 2027-28 volume terms for the second hyperscale agreement, adding to backlog (timing per management, not dated)
Belvidere, IL packaging facility operational; 2027 guide with Q4 results

ideas.valuation: At ~$224: ~25x 2026 EPS (~$8.98-9.20) and ~20-22x 2027 (~$10.1-11.5). Data-center power peers on the watchlist (VRT, GEV) trade materially higher. The average analyst target is ~$287-297 (Investing.com, Tickflow, late Jul), with UBS at $340.
ideas.estimate_revisions: Up. FY2026 EPS was ~$8.43 pre-Q2 (Barchart preview) and is ~$8.98-9.20 now. The 2027 range rose from ~$10.11 to as high as ~$11.46 (Stocksguide, late Jul). The C&I and margin guides were raised in July.
ideas.forward_growth: 2026 net sales guide is +mid-to-high teens. Consensus EPS ~+40% in 2026 (from $6.34) and ~+15-25% in 2027. Data center revenue goes from ~$450M (2026) to $1.35B+ of scheduled 2027 backlog. Sources: GNRC Q2 2026 8-K/call, Barchart, Stocksguide, Ticker League.
ideas.priced_in: 6-month +8% ($207.34 on Apr 9 to ~$224). +66% from the 52-week low ($134.80), -24% from the 52-week high ($296.44). Part of the data center story is priced, but the 2027 step-up, which is contracted and sits in backlog, is valued at ~20x. The second hyperscaler, potentially another ~$700M+, is not in numbers yet.
key_risks: Execution risk in scaling large-MW generator and packaging capacity; margin dilution from mix
Hyperscaler capex digestion or order-timing pushouts
Residential is still weak (-2% in Q2) and weather-dependent
Tariff refunds flatter 2026 margins (~150bp), so the underlying margin is lower
ideas.overlap_with_holdings: Moderate. Data-center power overlaps with VST (holding) and the VRT, GEV and BE watchlist names. About half of revenue is residential standby and clean energy, which diversifies.

ideas.name: StandardAero, Inc.
ideas.thesis: StandardAero is the largest independent engine MRO shop. Its LEAP and CFM56 programs turned profitable in Q2 2026, and it raised guidance for double-digit EPS growth, yet the stock sits at its 52-week low, about 13x 2026 EPS and ~10x EBITDA. The LEAP shop-visit wave (737 MAX at 47/month and A320neo deliveries up 10%) is a multi-year growth driver that the current multiple does not reflect.
ideas.why_now: Q2 2026 (Aug 6): adj EBITDA +12.3%, record 14.4% margin, adj EPS +24%, FCF positive, net leverage down to 2.6x from 3.0x, and FY26 revenue, EBITDA and EPS guidance raised (EPS $1.50-1.57). The stock nonetheless drifted ~16% lower after earnings and is ~41% off its high. Possible pressures: sponsor overhang (Carlyle/GIC sold 50M shares in January and still own ~40%), CEO share sales, and softer near-term air-traffic expectations. No single company-specific negative was found.

catalysts.event: Q3 2026 results (Q3 2025 reported Nov 10; 2026 date not yet announced)
FY2027 guidance with Q4 results: first full year with LEAP programs profitable
Boeing 737 rate step beyond 47/month and 737-7/-10 certification expected in 2026

ideas.valuation: At ~$20.35: ~13.3x 2026 adj EPS guide midpoint ($1.535) and ~12x 2027 consensus ($1.69). EV ~$9.0B (~334M shares, approx., plus $2.18B net debt) is ~10x 2026 EBITDA guide ($885-910M). Listed aerospace aftermarket peers (HEI, TDG, FTAI) have historically traded far above this; that comparison is the author's general knowledge, not sourced this week. The average target was ~$34 (MarketBeat).
ideas.estimate_revisions: Up. FY26 guidance was raised on Aug 6. FY26 consensus EPS is ~$1.50 versus a pre-raise ~$1.23 cited by MarketBeat, though the basis is not like-for-like because adj EPS now excludes all intangible amortization. FY27 consensus is $1.69 (+12.7%).
ideas.forward_growth: FY26 guide: revenue $6.375-6.5B (understated by $300-400M of eliminated pass-through revenue), EBITDA $885-910M (~+10%), EPS +double digits. Commercial aerospace is guided to grow low-double-digit to mid-teens. Consensus FY27 EPS is +12.7% (MarketBeat, Aug 2026).
ideas.priced_in: 6-month -24.5% ($26.93 on Apr 9 to ~$20.35). +2.5% from the 52-week low ($19.85), -41% from the 52-week high ($34.48). The multiple compressed from ~20x to ~13x while guidance rose, so the LEAP ramp is not in the price.
key_risks: Sponsor overhang: Carlyle and GIC still hold ~40% and have sold repeatedly
Air-traffic softness or airlines deferring shop visits if jet fuel stays high (Middle East conflict)
Customer and OEM-licence concentration (GE/CFM, Rolls-Royce, Pratt & Whitney); first-half FCF was negative
Military & helicopter ~15-20% of mix (not the main customer, but declined 2.6% in Q2); leverage 2.6x
ideas.overlap_with_holdings: Low with holdings. Thematic overlap with watchlist FTAI (CFM56/LEAP aftermarket) and UAL (air traffic); HWM, a past idea, is also aerospace. No overlap with tech or consumer holdings.

ideas.name: Regal Rexnord Corporation
ideas.thesis: Regal Rexnord's automation & motion segment is growing mid-teens (orders +17%), and ~$735M of E-Pod turnkey data center power orders (20%+ margins) begin shipping in early 2027, which should lift growth in 2027. The stock is ~15-16x 2026 EPS after a 34% drawdown on a small Q2 revenue miss.
ideas.why_now: Q2 2026 (Aug 5): adj EPS $2.99 vs $2.58 consensus, enterprise daily orders +8.8%, AMC organic +15.6%, FY EPS midpoint held at $10.60. Shares fell ~13-16% on a $20M revenue miss and the quality of earnings (tariff refunds). New CEO Aamir Paul is in place, and leverage is guided below 3.0x in 2H26.

catalysts.event: First E-Pod data center shipments (early 2027 per company)
2027 guidance with Q4 results: first look at E-Pod revenue contribution

ideas.valuation: At ~$164.5: ~15.5x 2026 adj EPS guide midpoint ($10.60), ~16.4x excluding $0.57 of tariff refunds. 2027 consensus is thin (~$13.6 per Tickflow, 2-3 analysts), implying ~12x. EV/EBITDA is ~10-11x with net debt/EBITDA of 3.06x. The average target is ~$245 (Tickflow, 11 analysts).
ideas.estimate_revisions: Flat to slightly down. The 2026 guide midpoint is unchanged at $10.60 versus ~$10.69 consensus, and KeyBanc cut its target from $265 to $240 on lower estimates. AMC orders (+17%) argue for upward 2027 revisions once E-Pod ships.
ideas.forward_growth: 2026 organic growth is low single digit (PES -6.6% offsets AMC +15.6%). 2027 thin consensus EPS ~$13.6 (+~28%, low confidence). Management targets ~$1B of power-management revenue within two years. Sources: RRX Q2 2026 8-K, Q4 2025 release (E-Pod $735M), Tickflow.
ideas.priced_in: 6-month -20.8% ($207.65 on Apr 9 to ~$164.5). +29% from the 52-week low ($127.96), -34% from the 52-week high ($247.80). The E-Pod backlog and AMC growth are valued at a cyclical-motor multiple, while the residential HVAC/pool trough is already in numbers.
key_risks: Leverage ~3x net debt/EBITDA limits flexibility
E-Pod execution: a new turnkey product with third-party content and project-management risk
Residential HVAC and pool weakness persists; rare-earth magnet supply and input-cost inflation
Low-quality 2026 EPS (tariff refunds); new CEO strategy reset
ideas.overlap_with_holdings: Low to moderate. Data center exposure overlaps the VST/VRT/ETN power theme, but most revenue is industrial motors, power transmission, automation and HVAC components, which diversifies away from tech holdings.
